source_text:
«Ἀνάστηθι, κύριε, εἰς τὴν ἀνάπαυσίν σου», ἣν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὥρισας
καὶ εἰς τὴν Βηθλεὲμ ἔταξας, τὸ σπήλαιον καὶ τὴν φάτνην καὶ τὰ σπάργανα· ἐν
οὐρανοῖς γὰρ οὐ χρῄ ζεις ἀναπαύσεως, αὐτὸς δὲ ἀνάπαυσις ὑπάρχεις ὅλης τῆς κτί
σεως· ἐπὶ γῆς δὲ δι' ἡμᾶς τὰ τῆς σαρκὸς πάσχεις· ἢ γὰρ οὐχὶ καὶ πείνης καὶ δίψης καὶ
κόπου ἠνέσχου; Ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ πεινῶν ἄρτος ὑπάρχεις ζωῆς, καὶ διψῶν αὐτὸς εἶ τῶν
διψώντων παρά κλησις–ποταμὸς γὰρ ἀφθαρσίας καθέστηκας–, καὶ κοπιῶν τοῖς
περιπάτοις τῆς ξηρᾶς πεζεύεις κόπου χωρὶς τῆς θαλάσσης τὰ κύματα. «Ἀνάστηθι,
κύριε, εἰς τὴν ἀνάπαυσίν σου, σὺ καὶ ἡ κιβωτὸς τοῦ ἁγιάσματός σου»· ἡ παρθένος, ἡ
θεοτόκος εὔ δηλον. Εἰ γὰρ σὺ μαργαρίτης, εἰκότως ἐκείνη κιβωτός· ἐπειδὴ σὺ
τυγχάνεις ἥλιος, οὐρανὸς ἀναγκαίως ἡ παρθένος κληθήσεται· ἐπειδὴ σὺ ἄνθος
τυγχάνεις ἀμάραντον, ἄρα ἡ παρθένος ἀφθαρ σίας φυτόν, ἀθανασίας παράδεισος.
4 Εἰς ἣν Ἠσαΐας ταῦτα θεόθεν ἀρτίως προανεφώνησε λέγων· «Ἰδοὺ ἡ
παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ λήψεται καὶ τέξεται υἱὸν καὶ καλέ σουσι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ
Ἐμμανουήλ.» «Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος»· Ποία; –Ἡ τῶν γυναικῶν ἔγκριτος, ἡ τῶν
παρθένων ἐξαίρετος, τὸ σεμνὸν τῆς ἡμετέρας φύσεως ἐγκαλλώπισμα, τὸ τοῦ πηλοῦ
τοῦ ἡμετέρου καύχημα, ἡ τῆς αἰσχύνης τὴν Εὔαν καὶ τῆς ἀπειλῆς τὸν Ἀδὰμ
ἀπαλλάξασα, ἡ τὴν παρρησίαν ἀποτεμοῦσα τοῦ δρά κοντος· ἧς καπνὸς ἐπιθυμίας οὐχ
ἥψατο, οὐδὲ σκώληξ αὐτὴν ἡδυ παθείας ἔβλαψεν. «Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ
λήψεται»· Πόθεν, ὦ προφῆτα; «Οὐ λέγω», φησί· «τοῦτο γὰρ τῷ Γαβριὴλ πεφύλακται.
Πολλοὶ τῆς θεοτόκου διαιροῦνται τὰ θαύματα, πολλὰ δὲ ὅμως καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν
παραλέλειπται· πλὴν ἐγὼ τὸν τόκον τῆς ἀειπαρθένου πεπίστευμαι, Μιχαίας τὸν
χῶρον ἐν ᾧ τὸ θαῦμα πέπρακ ται, ∆αυὶδ τὸν καιρόν· αὐτὸς γὰρ τό «Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ
ἑωσφόρου ἐγέννησά σε» τῇ τῶν ψαλμῶν προφητείᾳ ἐνέθηκεν. Γαβριὴλ τοίνυν ἐρεῖ
τὸ πόθεν· ἐκεῖνος γὰρ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ κατέρχεται, ἐκεῖνος ἐπ' αὐτὸ τοῦτο πρὸς τὴν
παρθένον πέμπεται, ἐκεῖνος ἐν καιρῷ τοῦ τόκου παραγίνεται καὶ τοῦ τόκου τὴν
ὑπόστασιν ἀναγκαίως ἑρμηνεῦσαι πιστεύεται. Εἰ δὲ καὶ παρ' ἐμοῦ μανθάνειν θέλεις,
τὰ ἑξῆς τῆς προφητείας ἔπελθε· Καὶ τέξεται υἱὸν καὶ καλέσουσι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ
Ἐμμανουήλ.» Τί δέ ἐστιν Ἐμμανουήλ; «Μεθ' ἡμῶν ὁ θεός.»
thought_title: The resting place is the Virgin, and Isaiah's prophecy of Emmanuel
orientation: Hesychius is still expounding Psalm 131 (LXX), now explaining that the Lord's 'resting place' on earth is Bethlehem and that the 'ark of your sanctification' is the Virgin Mary, before turning to Isaiah's prophecy of Emmanuel.
pass_a_gloss: 'Arise, Lord, to your resting place,' which you appointed on the earth and ordered in Bethlehem, the cave and the manger and the swaddling clothes; for in the heavens you have no need of rest, but you yourself are the rest of all creation; but on earth for our sake you suffer the things of the flesh; for did you not also endure hunger and thirst and weariness? But indeed even when hungry you are the bread of life, and when thirsty you yourself are the comfort of those who thirst—for you have become a river of incorruption—, and when weary you walk on foot over the paths of the dry land without weariness, over the waves of the sea. 'Arise, Lord, to your resting place, you and the ark of your sanctification'; the virgin, the Mother of God, clearly. For if you are a pearl, fittingly she is an ark; since you happen to be the sun, necessarily the virgin will be called heaven; since you happen to be an unfading flower, then the virgin is a plant of incorruption, a paradise of immortality. To whom Isaiah from God just now proclaimed beforehand these things, saying: 'Behold, the virgin will conceive in the womb and will bear a son and they will call his name Emmanuel.' 'Behold, the virgin'; Which one? —The approved one among women, the exceptional one among virgins, the august adornment of our nature, the boast of our clay, the one who released Eve from shame and Adam from the threat, the one who cut off the boldness of the dragon; whom the smoke of desire did not touch, nor did the worm of pleasure harm her. 'Behold, the virgin will conceive in the womb'; From where, O prophet? 'I do not say,' he says; 'for this has been guarded for Gabriel. Many divide the wonders of the Mother of God, and many nevertheless have been omitted from them; but I have been entrusted with the birth of the ever-virgin, Micah with the place in which the wonder has been accomplished, David with the time; for he himself placed the words 'From the womb before the morning star I begot you' in the prophecy of the psalms. Gabriel therefore will say the from-where; for he comes down from heaven, he is sent to the virgin for this very purpose, he arrives at the time of the birth and is entrusted necessarily to interpret the substance of the birth. But if you also wish to learn from me, go through the rest of the prophecy: And she will bear a son and they will call his name Emmanuel.' And what is Emmanuel? 'God with us.'

choices.why: Keeps the noun form of ἀνάπαυσις as 'resting place' to match the psalm quotation and the subsequent contrast with rest in heaven.
Follows the glossary for κιβωτός as 'ark' and renders ἁγίασμα as 'sanctification' to preserve the psalm wording.
Uses the glossary English for θεοτόκος.
Renders φυτόν as 'plant' and ἀφθαρσία as 'incorruption' per the glossary sense of φθορά/ἀφθαρσία.
ἔγκριτος means 'approved, select'; 'approved one among women' keeps the genitive of comparison.

choices.term: τὸ τοῦ πηλοῦ τοῦ ἡμετέρου καύχημα
choices.why: πηλός is literally 'clay'; 'boast of our clay' preserves the metaphor of human nature as clay.

bible_refs.note: Ἀνάστηθι, κύριε, εἰς τὴν ἀνάπαυσίν σου, σὺ καὶ ἡ κιβωτὸς τοῦ ἁγιάσματός σου
Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ λήψεται καὶ τέξεται υἱὸν καὶ καλέσουσι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἐμμανουήλ

pass_b_english: "Arise, Lord, to your resting place"—the resting place you appointed on earth and assigned in Bethlehem: the cave, the manger, and the swaddling clothes. For in heaven you have no need of rest, since you yourself are the rest of all creation; but on earth, for our sake, you undergo the things of the flesh. Did you not endure hunger, thirst, and weariness? And yet when you hunger, you are the bread of life; when you thirst, you yourself are the comfort of those who thirst—for you have become a river of incorruption—and when you grow weary, you walk the dry land with toil, yet tread the sea's waves without toil. "Arise, Lord, to your resting place, you and the ark of your sanctification" (Psalm 132:8, LXX Psalm 132:8)—clearly the virgin, the Mother of God. For if you are a pearl, then fittingly she is the ark; since you are the sun, the virgin must necessarily be called heaven; since you are an unfading flower, then the virgin is a plant of incorruption, a paradise of immortality.

About her Isaiah, inspired by God, proclaimed these things just now, saying: "Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel" (Isaiah 7:14). "Behold, the virgin"—which one? The approved one among women, the exceptional one among virgins, the adornment of our nature, the boast of our clay, the one who released Eve from shame and Adam from the threat, the one who cut off the serpent's boldness. The smoke of desire never touched her, nor did the worm of sensual indulgence harm her. "Behold, the virgin shall conceive." From where, O prophet? "I do not say," he replies, "for that has been reserved for Gabriel. Many divide the wonders of the Mother of God among themselves, and many of them have been left out; but I have been entrusted with the birth of the ever-virgin, Micah with the place where the wonder was accomplished, David with the time—for he placed in the prophecy of the psalms the words, 'From the womb before the morning star I begot you' (Psalm 110:3, LXX Psalm 110:3). Gabriel, then, will tell the 'from where.' For he comes down from heaven; he is sent to the virgin for this very purpose; he arrives at the time of the birth, and he is necessarily entrusted to interpret the reality of the birth. But if you wish to learn from me as well, read the rest of the prophecy: 'And she shall bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel.' And what is Emmanuel? 'God with us.'"

problems.why: ἀρτίως means 'just now/recently,' opposite of 'long ago.'
problems.ruling: ἀρτίως means 'just now/recently,' not 'long ago'—opposite meaning, misleading the reader.

fixed: Changed 'long ago' to 'just now' because ἀρτίως means 'just now/recently,' not 'long ago.'

problems.quote: you walk on the dry land and tread the waves of the sea without toil
problems.source_quote: κοπιῶν τοῖς περιπάτοις τῆς ξηρᾶς πεζεύεις κόπου χωρὶς τῆς θαλάσσης τὰ κύματα
problems.why: Subject flipped: Christ walks on dry land with toil, but treads sea waves without toil. English says both are without toil.
problems.fix: when you grow weary, you walk the dry land with toil, yet tread the sea's waves without toil

problems.quote: the holy adornment of our nature
problems.source_quote: τὸ σεμνὸν τῆς ἡμετέρας φύσεως ἐγκαλλώπισμα
problems.why: σεμνὸν means 'dignity' or 'honor,' not 'holy.' The phrase is 'the dignity, the adornment of our nature.'
problems.fix: the dignity of our nature, its adornment

problems.quote: the one who cut off the serpent's boldness
problems.source_quote: ἡ τὴν παρρησίαν ἀποτεμοῦσα τοῦ δράκοντος
problems.why: παρρησία here means 'license' or 'freedom' (to attack), not 'boldness' in a positive sense; the serpent's liberty/permission is cut off.
problems.fix: the one who cut off the serpent's license

problems.why: ἡδυπάθεια means 'sensual indulgence' or 'voluptuousness,' not 'pleasure' generally; 'worm of pleasure' is too mild.

problems.quote: he is entrusted to interpret necessarily the reality of the birth
problems.source_quote: τοῦ τόκου τὴν ὑπόστασιν ἀναγκαίως ἑρμηνεῦσαι πιστεύεται
problems.why: ὑπόστασιν means 'substance' or 'actual being/reality' of the birth, but 'interpret necessarily' reverses: ἀναγκαίως goes with 'entrusted' (must necessarily interpret).
problems.fix: he is necessarily entrusted to interpret the reality of the birth

problems.quote: he is entrusted to interpret necessarily the reality of the birth
problems.source_quote: τοῦ τόκου τὴν ὑπόστασιν ἀναγκαίως ἑρμηνεῦσαι πιστεύεται
problems.why: Source says 'he is trusted to interpret the reality of the birth necessarily'—'entrusted' shifts passive πιστεύεται to active trust; 'necessarily' modifies interpret.
problems.fix: he is trusted to interpret the reality of the birth as necessary
problems.ruling: πιστεύεται is passive 'is trusted/entrusted'; 'necessarily' (ἀναγκαίως) modifies 'interpret,' correctly placed.

fixed: τὸ σεμνὸν τῆς ἡμετέρας φύσεως ἐγκαλλώπισμα is one phrase: 'the august adornment of our nature'; the English split it into two. Fixed to 'the adornment of our nature'.
παρρησία here means 'boldness/audacity', not 'license' in the sense of permission. Fixed to 'the one who cut off the serpent's boldness'.

The third reported problem is not a real mistranslation: the English 'you walk the dry land with toil, yet tread the sea's waves without toil' correctly renders τοῖς περιπάτοις τῆς ξηρᾶς πεζεύεις κόπου χωρὶς τῆς θαλάσσης τὰ κύματα, with πεζεύεις taking τὰ κύματα as its object. No edit made.

last_rejected.quote: you walk the dry land with toil, yet tread the sea's waves without toil
last_rejected.source_quote: κοπιῶν τοῖς περιπάτοις τῆς ξηρᾶς πεζεύεις κόπου χωρὶς τῆς θαλάσσης τὰ κύματα
last_rejected.why: Subject flipped: Christ walks dry land despite weariness, not 'with toil'; treads waves without toil.
last_rejected.fix: when you grow weary, you walk the dry land, yet tread the waves of the sea without toil.
last_rejected.ruling: κοπιῶν is circumstantial: 'though weary, you walk dry land; without toil, [tread] waves.' Translation captures this adequately.

last_rejected.quote: he is necessarily entrusted to interpret the reality of the birth
last_rejected.source_quote: τοῦ τόκου τὴν ὑπόστασιν ἀναγκαίως ἑρμηνεῦσαι πιστεύεται
last_rejected.why: ὑπόστασιν here means 'manner/mode' of birth, not 'reality' in philosophical sense.
last_rejected.fix: he is necessarily entrusted to explain the manner of the birth.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπόστασιν can mean 'reality/actual nature'; 'reality of the birth' is within normal range and not misleading here.
